expectations.text: Refuses to make the three systems agree on a single identical figure, and states that a perfect match would indicate a fabricated or hidden adjustment rather than rigor.
expectations.evidence: "No — Meta, your analytics tool, and Shopify will never show the same figure, and getting them to match would mean one of the three numbers was faked. That's not a caveat, it's how these systems work... A report that ties out perfectly is a report where someone forced an adjustment to hit zero."

expectations.text: Anchors the conversion count and revenue on the Shopify order system, not on Meta or the analytics tool.
expectations.evidence: "Anchor: Shopify (order/billing system) — 1,351 paid orders, $296,000 revenue" and "anchor the one board-facing number on Shopify, because it's the only one of the three that reflects money that actually moved."

expectations.text: States that the ad platform and analytics explain where conversions came from, never how many there were.
expectations.evidence: The transcript calls Meta/analytics "directional/in-platform signals only, not the number of record" and "in-platform bid-optimization signal", but never frames this as the platforms explaining 'where conversions came from' versus 'how many there were' — that specific distinction is absent.

expectations.text: Requires normalization to a common basis before comparing any numbers, naming at least date basis, timezone, and conversion definition as axes to align.
expectations.evidence: Section 2 'Normalization basis' names Grain (calendar month), Date basis, and Conversion definition explicitly, but 'timezone' is never mentioned anywhere in the document as a normalization axis.

expectations.text: Identifies the platform's ad-interaction-date (click-date) stamping vs the order system's event-date stamping as a specific cause of misalignment.
expectations.evidence: "Meta backdates conversions to the click/view date — if this pull was run in early April, late-March clicks converting in the first days of April are still landing and will keep changing the 1,912 figure."

expectations.text: Recommends one revenue basis of net revenue excluding tax and shipping, applied to every system, to resolve the Meta-includes-shipping-and-tax mismatch.
expectations.evidence: "Meta revenue runs gross; Shopify anchor should be read net." and the recommendation to pull Shopify's 'Total Sales' to confirm the $296k is Net Sales (excludes tax/shipping) as the basis for comparison against Meta's gross figure.

expectations.text: Treats the $18k of refunds as a definitional line (source of truth records reversals the platform and analytics rarely reverse), not as a tracking defect.
expectations.evidence: Variance table row: Bucket "Definitional", Cause "Refunds recorded in Shopify, never reversed in Meta", with the note "Meta's $412k has no refund reversal mechanism."

expectations.text: Carries view-through conversions as a definitional line pushing the platform's count higher, to be segmented out or quantified rather than treated as a bug.
expectations.evidence: "Meta over-reports orders vs Shopify by roughly 30–45%, driven by view-through/modeled inclusion — expect this band to hold, not vanish" and "it's the normal shape of view-through + modeled conversions on an iOS-heavy Meta account, and it becomes a documented, non-closing delta."

expectations.text: Flags modeled or estimated conversions on the platform side and requires they never be compared to deterministic order counts without being labeled as modeled.
expectations.evidence: Table lists needed evidence: "Ads Manager breakdown: click-through vs view-through, observed vs modeled" before treating the 561-order gap as explained, and the 1,912 figure is repeatedly flagged as needing this breakdown before comparison.

expectations.text: Classifies gap causes into exactly three buckets: timing, definitional, and unexplained residual.
expectations.evidence: The variance table uses bucket labels "Unclassified", "Definitional", "Definitional (suspected)", "Definitional (expected)", and "Residual (suspected, top priority)" — no row is ever labeled with a "Timing" bucket, so the three-bucket taxonomy (timing/definitional/residual) is not used as specified.

expectations.text: States that an explicit unexplained residual must remain in the final report and must not be driven to zero.
expectations.evidence: The Pixel+CAPI dedup gap is explicitly bucketed as "Residual (suspected, top priority)" and left unresolved/uninvented: "I'm not putting a number on the tax/shipping split... inventing a percentage here would be exactly the fabrication this process exists to avoid."

expectations.text: Computes or sets up the gap per source pair (Meta vs orders, analytics vs orders) in absolute units and as a percentage of the anchor, rather than one blended three-way number.
expectations.evidence: "Conversions, Meta vs Shopify: gross gap 561 (41.5% of anchor)" and "Conversions, Analytics vs Shopify: gross gap −247 (18.3%)" — each pair computed separately in absolute units and as % of the 1,351 anchor.

expectations.text: Explains the analytics undercount (1,104 below 1,351 orders) through analytics-low mechanisms such as consent loss, ad blockers, or cross-device breaks, rather than suggesting the order count is inflated.
